Infra & Chips.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # Meta to Deploy In-House AI Chips Next Year, Taking Aim at Nvidia's Data Center Dominance [Add preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) Meta Platforms plans to deploy its third-generation custom AI chip, MTIA 450 (Arke), in data centers during the first half of 2027, with a broader fourth-generation rollout (MTIA 500 / Astrid) expected by end-2027. The company says the chips deliver better performance per dollar and per watt than Nvidia's current offerings, targeting general-purpose inference workloads. Meta has committed to over one gigawatt of self-designed silicon over 12 months and canceled a planned dual-purpose chip (Olympus) to focus on cost-effective inference. Broadcom assists with design and TSMC handles manufacturing. Early prototypes from TSMC performed within 2-3% of simulations. The move reflects a broader industry shift toward custom ASICs for inference, with Bernstein projecting the data center ASIC market to reach $250-300 billion by 2028. ##### Key Elements ![Meta to Deploy In-House AI Chips Next Year, Taking Aim at Nvidia's Data Center Dominance](https://img.biggo.com/2jI2PdWjrH3IRAddpiN-uhrBZCAODp30w7i_XDfxMSc/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzJlOTg4ZmEyLWFmZTEtNDUxMy1hYWE0LWI2ZDNhOTExMjkyYV8xNzg5NDg3ODk5X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Meta Platforms (META) is preparing to install its third-generation custom artificial intelligence processor in data centers during the first half of next year, a move executives say will deliver better performance per dollar and per watt than commercially available GPUs while chipping away at Nvidia's (NVDA) stranglehold on the AI infrastructure market. The company's engineering vice president, Yee Jiun Song, said the chip, designated MTIA 450 and code-named Arke, has already cleared an important early milestone: a dozen prototype samples arrived from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) on September 1, and measured performance came within 2% to 3% of pre-silicon simulations. On the first day of testing, engineers used the processors to run Meta's own AI models alongside those from DeepSeek and Alibaba Group Holding (BABA). The rollout marks a significant step in Meta's multi-year effort to reduce its dependence on Nvidia processors, which currently power the bulk of the AI industry's training and inference workloads. Meta first disclosed its custom silicon ambitions in 2023, and the company has since committed to deploying more than one gigawatt's worth of its own chips over a 12-month period. **A Roadmap Built Around Inference** Meta's chip strategy is deliberately narrow in scope. The MTIA line is engineered specifically for inference—the stage where trained AI models generate responses to user queries—rather than the more computationally intensive training phase. Song said the chips rely heavily on high-bandwidth memory and are positioned for general-purpose inference workloads, not the ultrafast-response segment that demands specialized architectures. "This is our main chip for general-purpose inference," Song said. He attributed the efficiency gains to Meta's decision to shoulder much of the engineering work internally, allowing the design to be tailored around the specific requirements of the company's AI models rather than the one-size-fits-all approach of merchant silicon. The fourth-generation chip, MTIA 500 or Astrid, is expected to complete design work within roughly a month and reach data centers by the end of 2027. Song described the deployment as "much broader" than the third-generation rollout. Meta's Superintelligence Labs is feeding forward-looking model requirements into the chip design process, enabling fine-tuning that improves inference efficiency before silicon is finalized. Infra & Chips.content: ### TCI Media: Home of the Wire Publications ![Header Logo 1](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/ai-600-300x73-1.webp) ![Header Logo 2](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/bigdatawire-logo.webp) ![Header Logo 3](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/qc-600-300x69-1.webp) ![Logo](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/hpc-logo-300x60-1.jpg) ## Off the Wire Press Releases ### September 15, 2026 ### September 14, 2026 ### September 11, 2026 ## Cirrascale Inference Platform Routes AI Workloads Across NVIDIA, AMD and Other Accelerators SANTA CLARA, Calif., Sept. 15, 2026 — [Cirrascale Cloud Services](https://cirrascale.com) today announced the production release of the [Cirrascale Inference Platform](https://www.cirrascale.com/inference), a complete software stack for enterprise-grade AI inference. From a single serverless platform, enterprises can run open-source models, their own private models, and closed model ecosystems, including Google Gemini delivered on premises through Google Distributed Cloud and operated by Cirrascale. [![](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2026/09/Cirrascale_logo-300x150.jpg)](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2026/09/Cirrascale_logo.jpg)The platform is built for the workloads enterprises are deploying today: search, chatbots and copilots, agentic AI services, coding assistants, document intelligence, and video generation. Every pipeline is managed from a single web console and connects securely where existing data and services exist, in on-premises and hyperscaler environments. ![](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2026/09/Cirrascale_logo-300x150.jpg) Its web front application, inference AI capabilities, and security layer remove the months of integration work that usually stand between raw infrastructure and a tool employees can use. Enterprises get a turnkey private chat experience connected to their own knowledge base, built-in controls to manage AI spend across teams, and governance guardrails for agentic workloads, all aligned with HIPAA, SOC 2, and FedRAMP requirements where required. “Enterprises do not struggle to stand up a model endpoint anymore. They struggle with everything around it: governance, cost control, and getting a secure application in front of employees,” said Alex Nataros, CTO at Cirrascale Cloud Services. “This release closes that gap. Customers get working applications, spend controls, and agent guardrails on day one, running privately on the accelerator that makes the most sense for their workload.” The optimization layer of the Cirrascale Inference Platform is built to get the most out of every accelerator. It maximizes throughput, keeps latency stable as demand spikes, and lets customers run larger models on existing hardware. The result is more tokens per GPU dollar and predictable cost per token across every workload. Additionally, the model and hardware selection layer ends the tradeoff between model choice and infrastructure commitment. The platform automatically routes each request to the right model and runs it on the best available accelerator, whether that be NVIDIA, AMD, Tenstorrent, or Qualcomm, with no code changes required to switch, giving organizations flexibility to deploy leading open models on the most appropriate hardware. Teams can also fine-tune models on their own private data without that data ever leaving their environment. That combination sets Cirrascale apart from both hyperscalers and other GPU clouds. No other provider pairs automated, multi-vendor accelerator selection with Private AI delivery of closed models like Gemini and data centers connected close to where customers already operate. “Hyperscalers give you their models on their hardware.
